topics.topic: PitchBook client mix shift toward Companies segment
topics.stated_position: Management said the client segment categorization was modified in 2019 and that "Since 2016, the Company client segment has exhibited the greatest expansion, and now represents about 30% of our total client count," describing Companies as "our fastest growing segment in the past 18 months" and "an extension of PitchBook's customer profile," while Core Investors "continue to be our largest source of new business bookings."
topics.quote: Since 2016, the Company client segment has exhibited the greatest expansion, and now represents about 30% of our total client count. Companies have also been our fastest growing segment in the past 18 months and represents an extension of PitchBook’s customer profile.

topics.topic: PitchBook total addressable market sizing and methodology
topics.stated_position: "We estimate that our total addressable market is $3.5 billion globally, an increase of approximately 52.2% since the $2.3 billion figure we shared at the 2020 Annual Meeting." Management attributes the increase to growth in Other Investor and Company categories and higher average revenue per client, and says a firm must be active in at least one supported use case to be counted, so the estimate captures clients that are "ready" rather than a "wish list."
topics.quote: We estimate that our total addressable market is $3.5 billion globally, an increase of approximately 52.2% since the $2.3 billion figure we shared at the 2020 Annual Meeting.

topics.topic: PitchBook long-term margin potential
topics.stated_position: "We continue to manage the business by balancing growth and profitability. PitchBook remains in growth-mode" and management believes that as PitchBook gains scale "PitchBook's profile will trend towards that of Morningstar's broader licensing areas." It declines to disclose product-level margins.
topics.quote: We continue to manage the business by balancing growth and profitability. PitchBook remains in growth-mode and we still believe there are substantial market opportunities for expansion

topics.topic: PitchBook competitive position versus S&P Capital IQ
topics.stated_position: Management observes Capital IQ "continues to pursue a partnership or acquisition strategy to build its private market data sets" and states "We believe PitchBook holds a competitive advantage in the market through our primary and secondary research processes and data coverage of areas important to our customers," citing a commissioned blind brand study in which PitchBook earned 33% of votes versus 7% for S&P Capital IQ.
topics.quote: We believe PitchBook holds a competitive advantage in the market through our primary and secondary research processes and data coverage of areas important to our customers.

topics.topic: Strategy for monetizing DBRS Morningstar credit data
topics.stated_position: Management agrees credit data is a growth opportunity with four dimensions — credit ratings data (RatingsNow), credit research, fixed income reference data (where "DBRS Morningstar does not offer a product in this area at present"), and normalized fixed-income credit data — and states the intent to replace third-party financial metrics with internal data across DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar and PitchBook.
topics.quote: We are currently working across DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar, and Pitchbook to replace third party sources of financial metrics with our own internal data. Our intent is that DBRS Morningstar’s normalized credit data can also be available through Morningstar Credit Information & Analytics (MCIA), Morningstar, and Pitchbook products in the future.

topics.topic: DBRS Morningstar EMEA growth plans
topics.stated_position: "Our immediate focus is on maintaining our very good coverage in the European structured markets (outside the CLO space) while building our footprint in fundamental ratings," with a specific objective to build demand for corporate ratings used for private placements and middle market lending, and progress cited in Spain, Italy and Portugal with momentum in France, Germany, the Netherlands and the UK.
topics.quote: Our immediate focus is on maintaining our very good coverage in the European structured markets (outside the CLO space) while building our footprint in fundamental ratings. With our existing ratings coverage of sovereigns and leading banks, our specific objective is to build the demand for corporate ratings used for private placements and middle market lending.

topics.topic: DBRS Morningstar relative profitability by region and margin ambition
topics.stated_position: Management says it feels comfortable with profitability in "leading" segments even though overall revenue is of modest size relative to larger competitors; Canadian margins benefit from more fundamental ratings and recurring revenue, while US and Europe core profitability is lower given transaction-based structured finance and ongoing investment. "Our goal, over time, is to turn more of our "established" market segments into "leading" segments, which we believe will favorably impact our margin profile."
topics.quote: Our goal, over time, is to turn more of our “established” market segments into “leading” segments, which we believe will favorably impact our margin profile.

topics.topic: ESG/Sustainalytics growth strategy
topics.stated_position: "Our growth strategy for Morningstar's ESG business encompasses three main avenues. The first is growing Sustainalytics' leadership position in ESG-related ratings, research, and data, the second is expanding Sustainalytics' position in sustainable finance, and the third is integrating Sustainalytics' IP into Morningstar's portfolio of offerings," with focus on expanding ESG data and research to wealth management and individual investors "which have been underserved historically."
topics.quote: Our growth strategy for Morningstar’s ESG business encompasses three main avenues. The first is growing Sustainalytics’ leadership position in ESG-related ratings, research, and data, the second is expanding Sustainalytics’ position in sustainable finance, and the third is integrating Sustainalytics’ IP into Morningstar’s portfolio of offerings.

topics.topic: ESG addressable market sizing
topics.stated_position: Management says published market size estimates range from several hundred million to several billion dollars and that most "understandably focus on the institutional investor market, which we believe is too limited a focus." "Sustainalytics and Morningstar aim to make ESG investing accessible to all investors, not just professional investors," with additional opportunity in the corporate market. "We continue to refine our understanding of that addressable market."
topics.quote: Furthermore, most published estimates of the ESG market size understandably focus on the institutional investor market, which we believe is too limited a focus. Sustainalytics and Morningstar aim to make ESG investing accessible to all investors, not just professional investors.

topics.topic: Integration of Sustainalytics onto Morningstar infrastructure
topics.stated_position: Management describes leveraging Morningstar technology at the corporate systems, technology operations, and product technology levels, with a "clear roadmap to complete this adoption by end of 2021," and says Morningstar's platforms have wide distribution to retail wealth "which is where we intend to increasingly surface and integrate Sustainalytics' ESG research and data."
topics.quote: From a customer reach standpoint, Morningstar’s platforms have wide distribution capability to the retail wealth customer segment, which is where we intend to increasingly surface and integrate Sustainalytics’ ESG research and data.

topics.topic: Sustainalytics differentiation versus MSCI
topics.stated_position: "The primary differentiator between Sustainalytics and MSCI is that the methodology underpinning Sustainalytics' ESG Risk Rating takes an absolute approach to highlighting risk, which allows investors to evaluate companies across sectors and geographies using consistent standards," contrasted with MSCI's sector-relative "best in class" scoring; management also cites work across the whole investment value chain and "one of the largest client service staffs in the industry."
topics.quote: The primary differentiator between Sustainalytics and MSCI is that the methodology underpinning Sustainalytics’ ESG Risk Rating takes an absolute approach to highlighting risk, which allows investors to evaluate companies across sectors and geographies using consistent standards.

topics.topic: Sustainalytics position in green/sustainable bond second party opinions and overlap with DBRS
topics.stated_position: Management cites Environmental Finance recognizing Sustainalytics as "the leading external reviewer of green/social/sustainability bonds with 36.5% market share," nearly equal to the next four competitors combined, and states "The products of Sustainalytics and DBRS Morningstar do not overlap in these efforts" — they are "complementary products for issuers."
topics.quote: The products of Sustainalytics and DBRS Morningstar do not overlap in these efforts, as the focus and meaning of a credit rating assigned by DBRS Morningstar differs from the second party opinion by Sustainalytics. We consider these complementary products for issuers.

topics.topic: ESG partnerships versus acquisitions
topics.stated_position: "we look at partnership and acquisition strategies separately. While we do not have an acquisition "wish list", Morningstar always surveys the landscape for value-creating acquisition opportunities." Management says the ESG landscape is "flush with interesting companies" but "there are no specific targets in our sights at the moment," and that developing strong partnerships is "an integral part of our business strategy."
topics.quote: To that point, we look at partnership and acquisition strategies separately. While we do not have an acquisition “wish list”, Morningstar always surveys the landscape for value-creating acquisition opportunities.

topics.topic: Morningstar Data growth drivers and data gaps
topics.stated_position: Management identifies four demand sources — regulation, data science and automation, changing technology platforms, and an evolving investor portfolio — says regulatory datasets including MiFID II "have made the most meaningful contribution to Morningstar Data's revenue growth over the past three years" with ESG datasets second, and names gaps including frontier market equity data, cryptocurrency and retail structured products.
topics.quote: Regulatory datasets, including those used to satisfy MiFID II requirements, have made the most meaningful contribution to Morningstar Data’s revenue growth over the past three years. ESG-related datasets have been the second strongest driver of revenue growth,

topics.topic: Morningstar Direct license renewal pressure and product transition
topics.stated_position: Management admits "we've experienced some pressure on license renewals as we work through evolving our legacy desktop-based product toward a flexible framework," cites a "gap of product market fit" for smaller wealth managers with three seats or less, and says it is challenged at large renewals by firms cutting expenses, especially asset managers facing consolidation and fee pressure.
topics.quote: At Morningstar Direct, even though we’ve seen consistency in new customer acquisition rates in recent years, we’ve experienced some pressure on license renewals as we work through evolving our legacy desktop-based product toward a flexible framework that enables the delivery of modern web components to both the desktop and web-versions of Direct.

topics.topic: Reason for moving Morningstar Direct to the cloud
topics.stated_position: "We decided to evolve the Morningstar Direct framework to the cloud to provide us and our clients with increased flexibility," enabling more frequent and efficient enhancements and client access "anytime, anywhere."
topics.quote: We decided to evolve the Morningstar Direct framework to the cloud to provide us and our clients with increased flexibility. Morningstar would be able to deliver enhancements to the products on a more frequent, more efficient basis, while our clients would be able to access our content anytime, anywhere.

topics.topic: Distribution-agnostic strategy and competition with FactSet and Bloomberg
topics.stated_position: "Morningstar has always taken the approach that the data, research, ratings and other content that we provide investors can and should be consumed however our clients want to consume it." FactSet and Bloomberg are competitors but also redistribute Morningstar data and pay to use it; "We have the ability to extract value from our offerings no matter the distribution channel."
topics.quote: Factset and Bloomberg are indeed competitors, but they also redistribute some of our proprietary data to their clients and pay us to use it in their products. We have the ability to extract value from our offerings no matter the distribution channel, which underscores the need we ultimately fill in the value chain.

topics.topic: Client stickiness and churn causes in Data and Direct
topics.stated_position: Management says its IP is embedded in client workflows, investment policies and compliance regimens, and "we believe that losing access to our IP is as much a source of the stickiness as the technical consequences of switching." "Churn in our core client base is more frequently due to consolidation or restructuring at our clients' firms and less so because of competitive dynamics."
topics.quote: Churn in our core client base is more frequently due to consolidation or restructuring at our clients’ firms and less so because of competitive dynamics, although that does happen from time to time. Generally speaking, however, the stickiness of our business model does have a protective effect against competition.

topics.topic: Key growth areas and investing "ahead of the curve"
topics.stated_position: Management identifies "key growth areas" as PitchBook, DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar Data, Morningstar Direct, Investment Management, and Workplace Solutions, representing "nearly 70% of our revenue," with Indexes and Sustainalytics named as other fast-growing areas of heavy investment, and an intent to invest in ESG-enabled solutions across the portfolio.
topics.quote: For some time, we’ve referred to our “key growth areas” as products that we believe have the potential to generate outsized growth, which includes PitchBook, DBRS Morningstar, Morningstar Data, Morningstar Direct, Investment Management, and Workplace Solutions. We’re fortunate that these product areas represent nearly 70% of our revenue

topics.topic: Expected five-year business mix and margin profile
topics.stated_position: "We've centered our efforts on continuing to support the development of differentiated products and solutions, investing for scale in multiple areas of our business, and expanding our leadership position in ESG across the portfolio." Management expects license-based areas to remain the largest revenue component for the foreseeable future and does not expect mix shift to be the primary driver of margin change; rather margins should improve "as we scale and benefit from operating leverage."
topics.quote: We have attractive growth opportunities across our portfolio but would expect our licensed based areas to continue to be the largest component of our revenue for the foreseeable future. Furthermore, we do not expect the primary driver of change in our margin profile to come from mix shift; rather, we’d expect to see our margins improve over time as we scale and benefit from operating leverage.

topics.topic: M&A priorities and process
topics.stated_position: "While we don't comment on our plans for future M&A, in the past we have made acquisitions to enhance our capabilities, particularly from a technology perspective, or to support growth in areas of the business where we see outsized potential." DBRS is cited as improving scale in credit ratings, Sustainalytics as supporting ESG product development, and AdviserLogic and PlanPlus as growing financial planning. Decisions weigh financial returns and strategic and cultural fit, and "our focus on organic growth means that we don't prioritize acquisitions for the sake of activity."
topics.quote: We have an established process to identify, evaluate, and prioritize acquisition opportunities. Our decisions are based on many factors with financial returns, and strategic and cultural fit being critical. Importantly, our focus on organic growth means that we don’t prioritize acquisitions for the sake of activity.

notable_language.quote: Incorporating use case assumptions into both our client count and average revenue per client assumptions assures that our estimate of the total addressable market accurately captures prospective clients that are “ready” to fully benefit from PitchBook’s offerings instead of simply representing a “wish list” of clients for whom our offerings may or may not resonate .
notable_language.why_notable: Management pre-emptively defends the credibility of a TAM figure it has just raised by more than 50% in one year, drawing a distinction between "ready" clients and a "wish list" — unusually defensive framing around a self-generated market estimate.

notable_language.quote: For smaller Wealth Management firms with three seats or less, price structure and competition on the Advisor’s desktop to complete specific workflows that are not currently offered in Direct result in a gap of product market fit.
notable_language.why_notable: An unusually direct admission of a product-market-fit gap and price disadvantage in a flagship platform, in a document that otherwise emphasizes competitive advantage.

notable_language.quote: While we do not disclose the exact estimates of our penetration of each category, it is fair to say that our penetration in the Core Investor client segments average in the high-teens for private equity, venture capital, and investment banks. We estimate that within Other Investors, a newer customer category, we have penetration in the mid-single digit range.
notable_language.why_notable: Rare quantification of market penetration, given only in approximate ranges and hedged with "it is fair to say" — the level of disclosure and its hedging are both notable.

notable_language.quote: While there are no specific targets in our sights at the moment, we will always consider acquisition opportunities that may arise with an eye toward accelerating our path to ESG leadership.
notable_language.why_notable: An explicit statement that there is no active ESG acquisition pipeline, paired with an open-ended willingness to act — a datable baseline for later transactions.

notable_language.quote: We still consider our Core Investor client segments to be venture capital, private equity, and investment banks; however, we recently added Other Investors into the Core classification.
notable_language.why_notable: Documents a redefinition of a reported client-segment category, which changes the comparability of previously disclosed client mix figures.

notable_language.quote: This requires robust data, research and ratings, along with access to a product shelf that includes ETFs, model portfolios, strategies, and CITs – it’s not just about mutual funds anymore!
notable_language.why_notable: Informal, emphatic phrasing signalling a self-described shift away from the mutual fund data heritage that has historically defined Morningstar.
